root_findings: The original stable-row conditions are equivalent, for p>=11, to the two stated q=1 and q=2 interval families; the identity 10M+1-b=(5j+5-q)p and the global bound b<=6M/7+1 are exact.
The stable raw coefficient is a convergent sum of disjoint interval lengths. It is a support ceiling, not a theorem about common-gate zeros.

For b>=M/5 the surviving interval lengths sum exactly to 1139587/9085230=0.125432927950..., exceeding the scoped 0.117797902016... per-M gap by 0.007635025933.... This prevents a capacity dismissal of the branch.
The stable eliminant has p-unit denominators on actual rows, and the b=900 factorization retains the required p=2399 cancellation witness.
The O(M log M) layer product, O(M^2 log M) inherited eliminant heights, and mock fixed sequence prove only the stated information barrier. They do not exclude a cancellation-aware cross-b invariant.
Item 149 already books the first rank-one copy. Common g0,g1 content can support at most one candidate extra first-gate copy and gives no A1 or third-copy implication.
Eight missing TeX spacing commands were repaired before resealing; no mathematical statement changed.
